To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Learning Analytics are a tool that, if not properly used, can lead to a homologating vision of the teaching and learning processes.
Learning Analytics, if not integrated into an inclusive approach, could have negative effects in terms of social exclusion.
Learning Analytics are an instrument that can be used for both formal and informal learning processes, and which is based on a behaviorist approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible effects that L.A. can have on the social inclusion of people with SLD or SEND.

understanding whether Learning Analytics can be considered as an inclusive approach, able to support the learning processes of all the students, including those with specific needs, or, on the contrary, if it can be considered as a tool that, by focusing on the performance, is able to identify the behavioural clusters that adhere to the predefined performance standards, thus ignoring the peculiarities of the individual.

a critical reflection on the use of Learning Analytics as a tool for the analysis of learning processes, with particular reference to the possible impacts that this approach could have on the social inclusion of students with SEND.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Learning Analytics, as an educational technology, has not been designed to support inclusive processes.

L.A. are not able to promote the inclusion of students with learning difficulties and/or disabilities, as they do not take into account the specificities of each student, nor do they consider the specific learning needs and the different cognitive styles.
Learning Analytics are not a tool that can be considered inclusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Learning Analytics, in the field of teaching, are a tool that, in the name of a supposed standard, risks to be a further instrument of exclusion, in a context in which the inclusive perspective is increasingly becoming a priority for the education system and the social community.
L.A. can be considered a tool that can be useful in academic learning contexts, but it is not a solution in itself.

L.A. are not able to guarantee a more inclusive teaching, because they are not able to identify the individual differences of the students and, therefore, to take into account the specific needs of each student.
The main takeaway from our work is that

L.A. is a technology that is still in its infancy and which, in the current state of the art, has the potential to be an instrument that can contribute to the exclusion of those students with SLD and SEND, who, due to their learning differences, are considered to be deviating from the standard of normality, and are thus excluded from the learning process.

Learning Analytics, if it wants to be considered as a valid tool in the educational sphere, should be used as an instrument to support the teaching and learning process, not as an instrument for control.
Learning Analytics, in its current formulation, is not a suitable tool for the educational inclusion of all students, including those with learning disabilities.
